major_issues.location: ## How Japanese People Learn the Pause — “Outdoor eating is already a special case.”
major_issues.problem: Overstates outdoor eating as special; contradicts Japanese everyday practice and the FAQ. The accurate uncommon pattern is eating while moving through a busy sidewalk.
major_issues.suggestion: Reframe: outdoor eating is common; walking-eating in commuter flow is the extra layer.

minor_issues.problem: Unsupported typical self-annoyance attributed to locals.
Three physical conditions vs four bold heads.
minor_issues.suggestion: Fix count or pull interpretation out of the list.

final_summary: PASS without a revision round: critical=0 and only one aggregated major, so the article was not patched. Legal and exception framing is sound (not a ban; festivals, ice cream, snack streets; outdoor eating exists; bins reinforce rather than cause the habit). The remaining major is a two-sentence overclaim that outdoor eating itself is a “special case.” Human editors may fix that line before publish; it does not fail the piece.
title: Why Japanese People Rarely Eat While Walking
